chunks: 926 - And in what al-Faḍl mentioned from the reasons, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, that he said:

“People were commanded to recite in salat (prayer) so that the Qur’an would not be abandoned and neglected, but rather be preserved and studied, so that it would not disappear nor be unknown. And al-Ḥamd was begun with, apart from the rest of the surahs, because there is nothing in the Qur’an and speech in which there has been gathered, from the comprehensive matters of goodness and wisdom, what has been gathered in Surah al-Ḥamd. And that is because His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He,”
“All praise is for Allah”
is only a fulfilment of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory upon His creation of gratitude, and gratitude for the good by which He granted His servant success.
“Lord of the worlds”
is tawhid (divine unity) for Him, praise of Him, and affirmation that He is the Creator, the Owner, none other than Him.
“The All-beneficent, the All-merciful”
is seeking His tenderness and mentioning His favors and blessings upon all His creation.
“Master of the Day of Judgment”
is affirmation for Him of resurrection, reckoning, and recompense, and affirming His dominion over the Hereafter just as affirming His dominion over the world.
“You alone we worship”
is desire and drawing near to Allah, exalted is His mention, and sincerity to Him in action apart from any other than Him.
“And You alone we seek help from”
is seeking increase in His granting success and His worship, and seeking continuity of what Allah has blessed him with and supported him by.
“Guide us to the straight path”
is seeking right guidance to His religion, holding fast to His rope, and seeking increase in recognition of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.
“The path of those whom You have blessed”
is emphasis in supplication and desire, and mention of what has already preceded of His blessings upon His awliya’, and desire for the like of those blessings.
“Not of those who are angered against”
is seeking refuge from being among the obstinate disbelievers who treat Him, and His command and prohibition, lightly.
“And not of those who have gone astray”
is seeking protection from being among those who went astray from His path without knowledge.
“While they think that they are doing good work”
So there has been gathered in it, from the comprehensive matters of goodness and wisdom concerning the Hereafter and the world, that which nothing else among things gathers.

And he mentioned the reason for which loud recitation was made in some prayers and not others: that the prayers in which recitation is done aloud are only in dark times, so it became necessary that they be recited aloud so that the passerby may know that there is a congregation there; if he wants to pray, he prays, because if he does not see a congregation, he knows that through hearing. And the two prayers in which recitation is not done aloud are only by day in bright times, so from the standpoint of sight there is no need in them for hearing.

Then when you have recited al-Ḥamd and a surah, say one takbir while you are standing upright, then bow, and place your right hand upon your right knee before the left, and place your palms upon your knees. Fit your fingers around the knee-joint and spread them, extend your neck, and let your gaze in ruku‘ be between your feet toward the place of your sajdah.

key_terms.تَوْحِيدٌ: Affirmation of Allah’s oneness and exclusive lordship.
key_terms.سُورَةِ ٱلْحَمْدِ: Surah al-Fatiha, described here as uniquely containing comprehensive goodness and wisdom.
key_terms.ٱلرُّكُوعِ: The bowing posture in salat (prayer), described here with its etiquette.
key_terms.ٱلْبَعْثِ: Resurrection after death, affirmed in the phrase about the Day of Judgment.
key_terms.ٱلْحِسَابِ: Reckoning of deeds in the Hereafter.
key_terms.ٱلْقِرَاءَةِ: Recitation in salat (prayer), prescribed so the Qur’an remains preserved and studied.

ai.seo_question: Why is Surah al-Ḥamd recited in salat (prayer), and why are some prayers recited aloud?
ai.summary: This hadith explains why recitation is prescribed in salat (prayer), why Surah al-Ḥamd is given precedence, and how its phrases gather foundational meanings of tawhid, gratitude, worship, guidance, and the Hereafter. It also gives the reason for loud recitation in certain prayers and concludes with instruction on the posture of ruku‘.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.926 - In what al-Fadl narrated from Imam al-Ridha (as) concerning reasons for the recitation in prayer, he stated: “People have been commanded to recite during prayer so that the Qur’an would not be abandoned or neglected, but instead preserved and studied so that it is neither forgotten nor lost. The recitation begins with Surah al-Hamd (The Opening) because it uniquely contains comprehensive wisdom and blessings not found in other verses of the Qur’an.
The phrase ‘Alhamdulillah’ (All praise is due to Allah (swt)) is a fulfilment of the obligation to thank Allah (swt) and an expression of gratitude for enabling His servant to do good.
‘Rabbil 'Alamin’ (Lord (azj) of the Worlds) affirms Allah’s (swt) unity, praise, and recognition that He is the Creator and Owner without any partner.
‘Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim’ (The Most Merciful, The Most Compassionate) is a plea for Allah’s (swt) kindness and a reminder of His blessings upon all creation.
‘Maliki Yawmid-Deen’ (Master of the Day of Judgment) is a declaration of belief in the resurrection, accountability, and Allah’s (swt) dominion over both worlds.
‘Iyyaka Na’budu’ (You alone we worship) signifies devotion and sincerity to Allah (swt) in worship.
‘Wa iyyaka nasta’in’ (And You alone we seek for help) seeks His continued assistance and favour.
‘Ihdinas-Siratal-Mustaqeem’ (Guide us to the Straight Path) asks for steadfastness in religion, adherence to divine guidance, and further recognition of Allah (swt).
‘Siratal-Ladheena an’amta ‘alayhim’ (The path of those whom You have blessed) expresses longing for the grace granted to Allah’s (swt) chosen ones.
‘Ghayril-maghdubi ‘alayhim’ (Not the path of those who have evoked [Your] anger) seeks protection from becoming among those who oppose or belittle Allah’s (swt) commands.
‘Wala-dhallin’ (And not of those who have gone astray) and [it is] a protection from being among those who have gone astray from His path without knowledge, thinking they are doing good. 
In this, all the essentials of goodness and wisdom, from both the matters of the world and the hereafter, have been combined in a way that nothing else can gather."
[AL SADUQ]
He the reason why loud recitation (Jahr) is prescribed in some prayers and not in others is explained. The prayers in which recitation is loud are done during dark times, so it is necessary to recite loudly so that people passing by can know that a congregation is present. If they want to pray, they can join. Without loud recitation, it would be hard for those passing by to know there is a congregation. The prayers in which recitation is not loud are performed in the daytime when it's bright, so they can be known through sight, and there is no need for hearing.
When you recite the Al-Fatiha and a Surah, you should say Takbir once while standing, then bow and place your right hand on your right knee before your left, with your palms on your knees. Spread your fingers around the knee joint, and extend your neck, keeping your gaze directed between your feet, toward the place of prostration."
